# `silk/cli/task`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Write a project's tasks in Silk: the program that `silk task <name>` and the manifest's
`[tasks]` hooks run.

## When to use
Put a project's automation, such as code generation, fixtures, release steps or checks before
`silk pack`, in `src/tasks.silk` instead of shell, Python or JavaScript scripts. The tasks are
the variants of a union that describes the command line with `silk.cli`, so `silk task` with no
name lists them, each task gets typed options, and a misspelled name gets a suggestion.

## Details
`silk task` builds the package's `tasks` profile, an executable for this machine whose root
module is `tasks.silk` unless `[profiles.tasks]` says otherwise, and runs it from the package
directory with the user's rights. The profile may add its own dependencies in
`[profiles.tasks.dependencies]`; they are fetched only when the tasks build. A package's tasks
never run where it is a dependency.

[`Task.main`](#Task.impl.main) reads the command line, runs [`TaskSet.perform`](#TaskSet.perform) on the chosen task, and turns a
[`TaskError`](#TaskError) into a one-line report and an exit status. [`Task.exec`](#Task.impl.exec) and [`Task.silk`](#Task.impl.silk) run
other programs with the terminal and environment of the task. A task that needs another task
calls it: tasks are ordinary functions.

The environment holds `SILK_PROJECT_ROOT`, the package directory; `SILK_INVOCATION_DIRECTORY`,
where the command was typed; `SILK_COMPILER`, the compiler that built the tasks; and, in a hook,
`SILK_HOOK`, such as `before-build`, and `SILK_HOOK_RESULT`, such as the `silk pack --json`
object after `silk pack`.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.cli.command { Command, CommandLine, Opt }
import silk.cli.task { Task, TaskError, TaskSet }
import silk.io.writer { WriterError }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.system.child_process { ChildProcess, ProcessError }
import silk.system.filesystem { FileError, FileSystem }
import silk.system.host_input { HostInput, HostInputError }
import silk.text.string { String }

union Tasks {
  Codegen,
  Release { pub version: String },
}

impl CommandLine for Tasks {
  static fn command() -> Command<Tasks> {
    return Command<Tasks>.make("tasks", "This project's tasks")
      |> Command.variant("Codegen", "Regenerate the tables")
      |> Command.variant("Release", "Test and pack a release")
      |> Command.arg("version", Opt.about("The version") |> Opt.required)
  }
}

impl TaskSet for Tasks {
  effect fn perform(self: Tasks) -> ()
    ! TaskError | ProcessError | FileError | HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError | WriterError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator | &mut ChildProcess | &mut FileSystem {
    match move self {
      Tasks.Codegen => run Task.exec("scripts/generate", &["--pinned"])
      Tasks.Release { version: _ } => {
        run Task.silk(&["test"])
        run Task.silk(&["pack"])
      }
    }
  }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ? &mut HostInput {
  return run Task.main<Tasks>()
}
```

<a id="Task.impl.main"></a>

### Associated function `main`

```silk
pub effect fn main<T: CommandLine + TaskSet>() -> i32 ? &mut HostInput
```

Reads the command line as `T`, runs the task it names, and answers the exit status: 0 when
the task succeeded, 0 after `--help`, 2 after a command line error, and a failed task's
[`TaskError.status`](#TaskError.status) after writing `error: <message>` to standard error. An unexpected failure,
such as a file that cannot be read, is reported the same way with status 1.

<a id="Task.impl.abort"></a>

### Associated function `abort`

```silk
pub effect fn abort(message: string) -> never ! TaskError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Fails the task with `message` and status 1.

<a id="Task.impl.exec"></a>

### Associated function `exec`

```silk
pub effect fn exec(program: string, arguments: &[string]) -> ()
    ! TaskError | HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator | &mut FileSystem
```

Runs `program` with `arguments` and waits for it. The program shares the task's standard
input, output and error, environment and working directory. A name without a `/` is looked
up on `PATH`; a path is relative to the working directory, the package directory.

#### Errors
[`TaskError`](#TaskError) when the program cannot be started, or ends with a nonzero status, which
becomes the error's status.

<a id="Task.impl.silk"></a>

### Associated function `silk`

```silk
pub effect fn silk(arguments: &[string]) -> ()
    ! TaskError | HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator | &mut FileSystem
```

Runs the compiler that built the tasks, `SILK_COMPILER`, with `arguments`, as [`Task.exec`](#Task.impl.exec)
does, such as `run Task.silk(&["test"])`.

#### Errors
[`TaskError`](#TaskError) when `SILK_COMPILER` is not set, or as [`Task.exec`](#Task.impl.exec).

<a id="Task.impl.capture"></a>

### Associated function `capture`

```silk
pub effect fn capture(program: string, arguments: &[string]) -> Bytes
    ! TaskError | ProcessError | HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError | WriterError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator | &mut ChildProcess | &mut FileSystem
```

Runs `program` with `arguments` to the end and answers its standard output. Its standard
error is passed on to the task's. The program starts in the package directory with no
environment but `PATH`, and a name without a `/` is looked up on `PATH`.

#### Errors
[`TaskError`](#TaskError) when the program cannot be found, or ends with a nonzero status or a signal.
